items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The Conte Grande was a 25,600 ton ship... Wilson Myers, bass.

ctx.x: When we set sail for France, Carol Dickerson of Chicago came to see us off, as he was a friend of Eugene Anderson, the ex-Cooper pianist. Most of the musicians in Lucky's band had been with Cooper.

Booker Pittman, Leroy Hardy, Alfred Pratt, R.H.'Mac' Horton, Henry Goodwin, Arnold Boling and myself. I had not played with the other members but knew them and they were Bill Dillard, trumpet, Arnold Adams, guitar and Wilson Myers, bass.

The Conte Grande was a 25,600 ton ship, and I was very excited about being on a big ship sailing for Europe and trying to picture what Monte Carlo and France would be like. We stopped in Boston and left there on 30th June and hit the high sea or the deep blue sea. In the dining room we were placed four at a table where there was a bottle of white wine and a little of red for each person.
